items.title: Clarence Ford Interview, 1975-12-10
items.q: Ray Charles played trumpet. He went with Ray Charles later on. I believe he wrote a couple of tunes for Ray Charles. ... Ray Charles got his thing from listening to guitar, Slim. And I never read anywhere where Ray Charles wrote that down. He got his thing because Ray Charles at the time was trying

ctx.x: Hospital? Yes. And we were talking about the musicians in your family before we ever had

the machine on. Well, far back as I know, my grandfather was a cornet player, Martin Gabriel. I was a drummer. And his sons, they all played, I believe. Martin Gabriel, I could call him Manny, my Uncle Manny. Uncle Clarence plays piano. Uncle Manny plays saxophone clarinet. He was a drummer with Louis Armstrong before he left New Orleans. And my Uncle August Lundwa, he married mine. He played bass. I know you know him. Uncle Clarence plays bass. And I was there, I have cousins. My Uncle had six boys and they all…
Yeah, I heard, I think, that, uh, a lot of people played across the river.
